limitations: Retrospective targeted selection, 15-second cutoff, three seeds; no full-corpus/default promotion claim.
Interval candidate counts are not feasible EUF/LIA model counts.
Equality decisions are outside the arithmetic inequality producer.
Counters align actual decisions to installed preference, not counterfactual beta; preference flips are not necessarily actual decision changes.
Region instrumentation adds bound/backtrack refresh work and measurable search-work overhead; no cost-free-policy negative result follows.
Persistent hint-context sampling differs from once-per-node randomized orientation in the supplied thesis.
Observed installed-sign alignment does not identify which eventual decisions differ from counterfactual beta.
Random and gated arms match flip probability per eligible context, not actual total override budgets.
conclusion: No new policy recovered any of the 30 recorded losses in any of three seeds. Native solved all losses; fixed-positive control recovered a subset. Geometry and gated policies did activate. Random-only perturbation also lost an easier control. Reject these policies for adoption on this evidence; interval geometry/history alone is not a demonstrated useful escape signal.
